descripcion_es: mine, yours, his, hers…; asking about the owner with whose.
resumen: Possessive pronouns (mine, yours, hers...) replace “possessive + noun” and stand alone, with no noun after them. To ask who something belongs to, use whose.

explicacion.texto: The determiner goes before a noun (This is my bag); the pronoun replaces it (This bag is mine). In Spanish it is the difference between “mi” and “(el) mío”. In English you never put the in front: the mine is wrong.

items: Possessives do not change with the gender or number of the thing owned: my brother, my sisters; it's mine, they're mine.
They do change with the owner: his (of a man), hers (of a woman), theirs (of them).
Hers, ours, yours and theirs have no apostrophe.
Its exists as a determiner (its tail) but is almost never used as a pronoun.

explicacion.texto: Whose = who does it belong to? It can go with a noun (Whose car is this?) or alone (Whose is this?). Don't confuse it with who's (= who is).
Useful expression: a friend of mine = one of my friends (es: un amigo mío); a cousin of hers = one of her cousins (es: un primo suyo).

ejemplos.frase: Their garden is bigger than ours.
ejemplos.traduccion: Su jardín es más grande que el nuestro.

ejemplos.frase: That's not my phone. Mine is black.
ejemplos.traduccion: Ese no es mi móvil. El mío es negro.

ejemplos.frase: A friend of mine works in Brussels.
ejemplos.traduccion: Un amigo mío trabaja en Bruselas.

errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Possessive pronouns do not take the.
The possessive agrees with the owner (Maria → her), not with the thing owned.
Who's = who is; to ask about the owner, use whose.

ejercicios.frase: That bike belongs to Peter. It's ___.
ejercicios.explicacion: Use the possessive pronoun column in the table: the pronoun for he is his, which here is the same as the determiner. The clue is the owner, Peter (a man, he), and the gap at the end, with no noun after it. That is why Spanish “es suya” is It's his. Remember that the pronoun agrees with the owner, not with the bike.
ejercicios.traduccion: Esa bici es de Peter. Es suya.

errores_previstos.explicacion: This copies the gender of Spanish “bici” (“suya”): in English the possessive depends on the owner, Peter, who is male.
Him is the object pronoun; for possession you need his.
His already works as a possessive pronoun and needs nothing added.

ejercicios.explicacion: Use the table of possessive pronouns: the pronoun for they is theirs. The clue is the hint (they) and the gap at the end, replacing their car, which is not repeated. That is why it is theirs, with no article in front (although Spanish says “el suyo”) and no apostrophe.
ejercicios.traduccion: Este es nuestro coche, no el suyo (de ellos).

errores_previstos.explicacion: Their is the determiner and needs a noun after it (their car); alone, use theirs.
A calque of Spanish “el suyo”: the English possessive pronoun never takes an article.
Theirs has no apostrophe.

ejercicios.explicacion: Use the table of possessive pronouns: the pronoun for you is yours. The clue is that we are speaking directly to Lucy (her name at the start), so the owner is you; and the gap is at the end, with no noun. That is why it is yours. Although Lucy is a woman, you don't use hers, because you are speaking to her.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The question is to Lucy (you): yours.

errores_previstos.explicacion: We are speaking to Lucy, not about Lucy: the second person is yours.
Your goes with a noun (your jacket); at the end of the sentence you need yours.
Yours has no apostrophe.

ejercicios.frase: We can't use your printer because ___ is broken. (we)
ejercicios.explicacion: Use the table of possessive pronouns: the pronoun for we is ours. The clue is the hint (we) and the gap before the verb is, as the subject, replacing our printer. That is why it is ours, with no article, unlike Spanish “la nuestra”.
ejercicios.traduccion: No podemos usar tu impresora porque la nuestra está rota.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Our needs a noun after it (our printer); to replace it, use ours.
A calque of Spanish “la nuestra”: the possessive pronoun takes no article.
Ours has no apostrophe.

ejercicios.explicacion: Use the part of the card about whose, which asks who something belongs to. The clue is that a noun (shoes) comes after the gap and the sentence asks about the owner. Whose can be followed by a noun, as here. Who's is the contraction of who is and would make no sense: “who is shoes are these” is not a sentence.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Who's = who is; to ask about the owner you use whose, which sounds the same but is spelt differently.
Who asks about a person; to ask about the owner you need whose.
A calque of Spanish “¿de quién?”: in English you say whose, with no preposition.

ejercicios.frase: Anna says the blue suitcase is ___.
ejercicios.explicacion: Use the difference between the determiner her and the pronoun hers. The clue is that the gap is at the end, with no noun after it, and the owner is Anna, a woman. That is why you need the female pronoun hers, which has no apostrophe.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: It stands alone, with no noun: hers.
ejercicios.traduccion: Anna dice que la maleta azul es suya.

por_opcion.her: Incorrect: her is a determiner (her suitcase) or an object pronoun; at the end of the sentence, replacing the noun, use hers.
por_opcion.hers: Correct: the possessive pronoun for she, alone and with no apostrophe.
por_opcion.her's: Incorrect: possessive pronouns have no apostrophe.

ejercicios.frase: I forgot my pen. Can I borrow ___?
ejercicios.explicacion: Use the rule that the possessive pronoun replaces “possessive + noun” and never takes an article. The clue is that there is no noun after the gap: pen was already said in the previous sentence. That is why your pen becomes yours. Borrow means to take something for a short time: Can I borrow yours? is Spanish “¿me prestas el tuyo?”.
ejercicios.traduccion: Se me ha olvidado el boli. ¿Me dejas el tuyo?

por_opcion.your: Incorrect: your needs a noun after it (your pen).
por_opcion.yours: Correct: it replaces your pen without repeating the noun.
por_opcion.the yours: Incorrect: a calque of Spanish “el tuyo”; in English the possessive pronoun never takes the.

ejercicios.explicacion: Use the useful expression on the card: a friend of mine (es: un amigo mío). The structure is a + noun + of + possessive pronoun. The clue is the preposition of, which in this construction is followed by the possessive pronoun, not the object pronoun. That is why it is a colleague of mine. “A colleague of me” is a common mistake, copied from Spanish “de mí”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The structure is a colleague of mine.

por_opcion.me: Incorrect: after of in this structure you use the possessive pronoun, not the object pronoun: of mine.
por_opcion.my: Incorrect: my needs a noun after it.
por_opcion.mine: Correct: the fixed structure a colleague of mine (es: un compañero mío).

glosario.definicion_l: an associate that one works with · a person who is member of one's class or profession

ejercicios.frase: The children are playing with ___ toys.
ejercicios.explicacion: Use the difference between determiner and pronoun explained on the card: the determiner goes before a noun and the pronoun replaces it. The clue is that the noun toys comes after the gap, so you need the determiner their. Theirs would only be possible with no noun after it (The toys are theirs).
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: It goes before a noun: the determiner their.
ejercicios.traduccion: Los niños están jugando con sus juguetes.

por_opcion.theirs: Incorrect: theirs stands alone; with toys after it you need the determiner their.
por_opcion.their: Correct: the possessive determiner for they, before the noun toys.
por_opcion.they: Incorrect: they is the subject pronoun and does not express possession.

ejercicios.enunciado: Rewrite the sentence with a possessive pronoun.
ejercicios.explicacion: Use the card's rule that the pronoun replaces “possessive + noun”: my seat becomes mine. To transform it, the noun seat moves next to this (This seat) and the pronoun mine goes at the end, alone. The clue is the instruction to use a possessive pronoun, which forces you to take the noun away from after the possessive.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: My seat → mine, at the end and with no noun.

errores_previstos.explicacion: My needs a noun after it; at the end of the sentence use mine.
A calque of Spanish “el mío”: mine takes no article.
Me is the object pronoun and changes the meaning (“this seat is me”); for possession, use mine.

ejercicios.enunciado: Ask the question with whose to find out the owner.
ejercicios.explicacion: Use the part of the card about whose: it can go with a noun (Whose phone is this?) or alone (Whose is this?). The clue is the instruction to find out the owner of somebody's phone: we are asking about the owner. The most natural form is Whose phone is this?; Whose is this phone? and Whose is this?, with whose alone as a pronoun, are also accepted.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Who's = who is; to ask about the owner you write whose.
A calque of Spanish “¿de quién es este teléfono?”: in English you use whose, with no preposition.
In a question the verb goes before the subject: Whose phone is this?

ejercicios.explicacion: Use the card's rule that in English you never put the before a possessive pronoun. The mistake is a calque of Spanish “los nuestros”. The clue is that ours is already a complete pronoun and needs no article. Just remove the: Those books aren't ours, or with the full negative, are not ours.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: No the before the possessive pronoun.

errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: the possessive pronoun takes no article.
The article has been removed but the pronoun has been changed to the determiner: our needs a noun; alone, use ours.
It keeps the article and uses the determiner: you need the two opposite changes, no the and ours.

ejercicios.frase: My sister lives with his husband in Bilbao.
respuestas: My sister lives with her husband in Bilbao.
ejercicios.explicacion: Use the card's rule that possessives change with the owner: his (of a man), her (of a woman). The husband's owner is my sister, a woman, so it is her. The mistake comes from thinking of the thing owned (husband, male), as Spanish does with gender. The clue is to ask whose husband it is: my sister's, so her.
ejercicios.traduccion: Mi hermana vive con su marido en Bilbao.

errores_previstos.respuesta: My sister lives with his husband in Bilbao.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: his would mean the husband belongs to a man; the owner is my sister, so her.

errores_previstos.respuesta: My sister lives with hers husband in Bilbao.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Hers stands alone; before a noun use her.

errores_previstos.respuesta: My sister lives with the her husband in Bilbao.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The possessive does not combine with the article.

ejercicios.enunciado: Put the words in order to make a question.
ejercicios.explicacion: Use the card's structure for whose: Whose + noun + is this? The clue is that whose asks about the owner and, when it goes with a noun, they form a block that cannot be separated at the start of the question (whose coat); then comes the verb is and then the subject this. Whose is this coat?, with whose alone, is also accepted.

errores_previstos.explicacion: In a question the verb goes before the subject: is this, not this is.
In English, question words go at the start of the question.
This is the order of an affirmative sentence: whose must go at the start and the verb before this.

ejercicios.explicacion: Use the rule that the possessive pronoun goes without a noun. The clue is the word one, which replaces the object we are talking about (the red one, es: “el rojo”): this way the adjective red is not left alone. You can order it as The red one is mine or as Mine is the red one, because mine works like a noun and can be the subject or the complement.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The possessive pronoun goes without a noun.

errores_previstos.explicacion: A calque of Spanish “el rojo” with the adjective after it: in English the adjective goes before one, the red one.
Mine takes no article, and the must go with red one.
The article goes at the start of the group: the red one. The adjective cannot go before the.

descripcion_larga_es: Possessive pronouns (mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs) replace “possessive + noun” and stand alone: This bag is mine. With them you also learn whose, to ask who something belongs to, and the expression a friend of mine. Spanish speakers find it hard not to add an article (“the mine”, a calque of “el mío”) and to tell whose from who's.

contexto.que_es: They are the words that replace a possessive determiner plus its noun: my book becomes mine, her bag hers, their car theirs. They always stand alone, with no noun after them and no article in front. They are completed by whose, which asks about the owner, and by the structure a friend of mine (es: un amigo mío).
contexto.por_que_importa: They let you avoid repeating the noun, which is very common when comparing or making clear who something belongs to (Is this yours? No, mine is black). The typical mistakes (“the mine”, “her's”, “a friend of me”) are very noticeable. Also, confusing whose and who's is a common spelling mistake that is penalised in written work.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: When the noun has already been mentioned or is understood: when giving things back, comparing belongings or answering whose. The signal is that there is no noun after the gap (it goes at the end of the sentence or before the verb). Spanish speakers tend to add an article, as in “el mío”, and to confuse the determiner and the pronoun.
